source: Based on the Cedars-Sinai "Low Fermentation Diet / SIBO Diet" handout by Mark Pimentel, M.D. Items marked "Not in the handout" are best guesses: check with your doctor.

foods.name: Chicken
foods.note: All proteins are good on this diet.

foods.name: Turkey
foods.note: All proteins are good on this diet.

foods.name: Beef
foods.note: Fine. At steakhouses, meat is often cooked with butter, which has lactose.

foods.name: Pork
foods.note: All proteins are good on this diet.

foods.name: Lamb
foods.note: All proteins are good on this diet.

foods.name: Fish
foods.note: Fish and seafood are fine.

foods.name: Eggs
foods.note: Eggs are great.

foods.name: Protein powder
foods.note: Fine, including whey, unless sweetened with sucralose or a sugar alcohol.

foods.name: Tofu
foods.note: Not in the handout. Soy is a legume, and the handout says no beans or legumes.

foods.name: White rice
foods.note: Rice, potatoes and sweet potatoes are the best carbs.

foods.name: Brown rice
foods.note: Not in the handout. Whole grains have more fiber than white rice.

foods.name: Potatoes
foods.note: Rice, potatoes and sweet potatoes are the best carbs.

foods.name: Sweet potatoes
foods.note: Rice, potatoes and sweet potatoes are the best carbs.

foods.name: White bread
foods.note: White, sourdough, Italian, French and potato bread are fine.

foods.name: Whole wheat bread
foods.note: Avoid whole wheat and multigrain breads.

foods.name: Pasta
foods.note: Pasta is all fine.

foods.name: Rice Krispies
foods.note: Rice Krispies are the most ideal breakfast cereal.

foods.name: Cheerios
foods.note: Many cereals now have added fiber. Watch for it.

foods.name: Cream of wheat
foods.note: For a hot cereal, choose cream of wheat over oatmeal.

foods.name: Oatmeal
foods.note: Skip oatmeal. Choose cream of wheat instead.

foods.name: Fiber supplements
foods.note: Do not go out of your way to eat fiber or fiber supplements.

foods.name: Quinoa
foods.note: Not in the handout. Less simple than rice and potatoes.

foods.name: Rye bread
foods.note: Not in the handout. The handout says white breads, and to avoid whole wheat and multigrain.

foods.name: Olive oil
foods.note: Fats are allowed. Bacteria cannot digest fat on its own.

foods.name: Butter
foods.note: Butter contains lactose. Small amounts.

foods.name: Onion
foods.note: Anything that grows under the ground is fine, including onions.

foods.name: Garlic
foods.note: Anything that grows under the ground is fine, including garlic.

foods.name: Carrots
foods.note: Anything that grows under the ground is fine.

foods.name: Beets
foods.note: Anything that grows under the ground is fine.

foods.name: Turnips
foods.note: Anything that grows under the ground is fine.

foods.name: Tomato
foods.note: Fruit vegetables like tomatoes are fine.

foods.name: Cucumber
foods.note: Fruit vegetables like cucumber are fine.

foods.name: Zucchini
foods.note: Zucchini and squash are fine.

foods.name: Bell pepper
foods.note: Peppers are fine.

foods.name: Eggplant
foods.note: Eggplant is fine.

foods.name: Peas
foods.note: Peas are fine, but not the pod.

foods.name: Snap peas
foods.note: Peas are fine, but not the pod.

foods.name: Corn
foods.note: Grows off a plant, like the other fruit vegetables.

foods.name: Green beans
foods.note: Not in the handout. They are a bean pod. The handout says no beans or legumes.

foods.name: Mushrooms
foods.note: Mushrooms are all good.

foods.name: Olives
foods.note: Grows off a plant. Fine.

foods.name: Celery
foods.note: Not in the handout.

foods.name: Leek
foods.note: Not in the handout. Related to onion, but mostly grows above ground.

foods.name: Asparagus
foods.note: Not in the handout.

foods.name: Lettuce
foods.note: A side salad is fine, not a salad as the meal. Best salad: tomato, cucumber and onion.

foods.name: Spinach
foods.note: Leafy vegetables only as a side, not the main dish.

foods.name: Broccoli
foods.note: Avoid broccoli.

foods.name: Cauliflower
foods.note: Avoid cauliflower.

foods.name: Cabbage
foods.note: Avoid cabbage.

foods.name: Brussels sprouts
foods.note: Avoid Brussels sprouts.

foods.name: Beans
foods.note: No beans or legumes. They contain a sugar bacteria ferment into gas.

foods.name: Hummus
foods.note: No hummus. The handout calls it the worst for SIBO.

foods.name: Lentils
foods.note: No beans or legumes.

foods.name: Nuts
foods.note: Nuts are all fine.

foods.name: Peanut butter
foods.note: Nuts are all fine, so peanut butter is fine.

foods.name: Chia seeds
foods.note: Not in the handout. Mostly fiber. The handout says not to go out of your way for fiber.

foods.name: Strawberries
foods.note: All fruits other than apples, pears and bananas are fine.

foods.name: Blueberries
foods.note: All fruits other than apples, pears and bananas are fine.

foods.name: Oranges
foods.note: All fruits other than apples, pears and bananas are fine.

foods.name: Lemon
foods.note: Fine.

foods.name: Grapes
foods.note: All fruits other than apples, pears and bananas are fine.

foods.name: Pineapple
foods.note: All fruits other than apples, pears and bananas are fine.

foods.name: Melon
foods.note: All fruits other than apples, pears and bananas are fine.

foods.name: Avocado
foods.note: A fruit. All fruits other than apples, pears and bananas are fine.

foods.name: Banana
foods.note: Constipating and slows the gut. Eat at a minimum.

foods.name: Apple
foods.note: Constipating and slows the gut. Eat at a minimum.

foods.name: Pear
foods.note: Constipating and slows the gut. Eat at a minimum.

foods.name: Dried fruit
foods.note: Not in the handout. Fruit is allowed, but dried fruit is concentrated fruit sugar.

foods.name: Lactose-free milk
foods.note: Use Lactaid milk. The lactose is already broken down.

foods.name: Milk
foods.note: Regular milk has lactose.

foods.name: Yogurt
foods.note: No yogurt. It has lactose and live bacteria.

foods.name: Cheese
foods.note: Cheese has lactose.

foods.name: Hard cheese
foods.note: A cheat on rare occasions. Aged hard cheese is much lower in lactose.

foods.name: Ice cream
foods.note: Has lactose.

foods.name: Lactose-free ice cream
foods.note: A cheat on rare occasions. Watch for sucralose.

foods.name: Sour cream
foods.note: Dairy with lactose.

foods.name: Sugar
foods.note: Regular sugar is fine, so cake and cookies made with it are fine.

foods.name: Dark chocolate
foods.note: Chocolate is allowed. Watch for milk chocolate.

foods.name: Milk chocolate
foods.note: Contains milk, so lactose.

foods.name: Honey
foods.note: Mostly fructose, which is harder to digest and feeds bacteria.

foods.name: High-fructose corn syrup
foods.note: Fructose is harder to digest and feeds bacteria.

foods.name: Aspartame
foods.note: NutraSweet (Equal) is a short protein, not a sugar. Perfectly OK.

foods.name: Sucralose
foods.note: Humans cannot digest it, so it all goes to the bacteria.

foods.name: Sugar alcohols
foods.note: Avoid anything with alcohol sugars. Names often end in -ol.

foods.name: Gum
foods.note: Gum is the biggest problem, usually because of sorbitol.

foods.name: Water
foods.note: Drink 5 to 8 cups of liquid a day.

foods.name: Soda
foods.note: Minimize soda. Diet soda with aspartame is OK; check the label for sucralose.

foods.name: Coffee
foods.note: Not in the handout. Plain coffee or tea has no sugar. Watch milk and sweeteners.

foods.name: Probiotics
foods.note: All bacteria ferment and make gas, including probiotic bacteria.
